title: Analyzing HPC Utilization with PIKA and Vampir
problem: Analyzing cluster-level HPC resource utilization requires bridging site-level monitoring data from tools like PIKA with application-level performance analysis tools like Vampir. Current tools operate at different abstraction levels and cannot easily share or transform data across these levels.
motivation: Comprehensive understanding of HPC cluster utilization patterns is essential for optimizing resource allocation and identifying performance bottlenecks in large-scale computing systems.
method: The approach extends both PIKA (site-level monitoring) and Vampir (application-level performance analysis) to enable cluster-level analysis. Site-level monitoring data is transformed into formats compatible with application-level tools, allowing these tools to analyze aggregate cluster behavior. The transformation bridges the abstraction gap between site-level and application-level monitoring.
key_novelty: A systematic data transformation methodology that bridges site-level monitoring tools with application-level performance analysis frameworks to enable cluster-level behavioral analysis.
contributions: Extension of PIKA for comprehensive site-level HPC monitoring
Extension of Vampir to support cluster-level data analysis
Data transformation approach converting site-level to application-level formats
Demonstration of cluster behavior analysis capabilities using transformed data
